facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes
A 63-year-old man presented with an asymptomatic, new-onset eruptive facial lesion
chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome
refractory anemia with excess blasts
a 3×2–mm smooth, red, dome-shaped papule under the right lower eyelid
A shave biopsy specimen demonstrated a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells
uniformly positive for CD207/langerin
negative for myeloperoxidase
BRAF-V600E variant status was identified through immunohistochemical studies
Prior bone marrow biopsy specimens showed hypercellular bone marrow with atypical erythropoiesis and 10% to 15% myeloblasts

Next-generation sequencing targeted extensive gene profiles in the bone marrow aspirate and paraffin-embedded skin biopsy specimens revealed identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes

concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells, uniformly positive for CD207/langerin, which is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The patient's history of chronic high-grade myelodysplastic syndrome and refractory anemia with excess blasts, combined with the skin biopsy findings, suggests myelodysplastic syndrome-associated skin infiltration.
The patient's skin lesion and biopsy findings, in combination with his history of myelodysplastic syndrome, are consistent with leukemia cutis.

The patient's skin biopsy showed BRAF-V600E variant status, which is consistent with a melanocytic proliferation, although the clinical context suggests a possible association with his underlying hematologic malignancy.

rationales.F05: The presence of a diffuse atypical dermal infiltrate of monocytoid-appearing cells is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F06: The uniform positivity for CD207/langerin is a specific marker for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F08: The presence of the BRAF-V600E variant is a characteristic feature of BRAF-V600E-positive melanocytic proliferation.
rationales.F10: The identification of identical pathogenic variations in the ASXL1, IDH2, and STAG2 genes in both bone marrow and skin biopsy specimens suggests a clonal relationship between the two, supporting a diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis or myelodysplastic syndrome-associated skin infiltration.
